Title: Tawau Port acquires two new dock cranes worth RM70mil
Article:
TAWAU: The acquisition of two new quay cranes worth RM70 million for Tawau Port is expected to boost port efficiency and strengthen its role as a key maritime gateway on Sabah's east coast.
Sabah Chief Minister Datuk Seri Hajiji Noor said the investment is a strategic step to strengthen the state's port infrastructure and support Sabah's long-term economic growth.
He noted that the investment also reflects the state government's commitment through Sabah Ports Sdn Bhd (SPSB) to modernise critical infrastructure, enhancing efficiency and competitiveness of Sabah's ports, particularly on the state's east coast.
"When they become operational, these cranes are expected to improve productivity, operational reliability, and overall cargo-handling efficiency at Tawau Port.
"They will also shorten vessel turnaround times, reduce waiting times, and strengthen the port's capacity to handle larger ships and increasing cargo volumes," he said during the launch of the new cranes at Tawau Port today.
Hajiji emphasised that an efficient and resilient port system is crucial to supporting the growth of key sectors, especially export-oriented industries that contribute significantly to the state's economy.
He said the Tawau Port upgrade is expected to continue fortifying its role as a major maritime gateway on Sabah's east coast, while enhancing connectivity with domestic and regional markets.
The chief minister also praised SPSB, Suria Capital Holdings Bhd, and all parties involved for their ongoing commitment to enhancing the state's maritime infrastructure to support its development agenda.
Meanwhile, Suria Capital chairman Datuk Seri Abdul Rahman Dahlan said the investment reflects the group's long-term commitment to developing strategic infrastructure.
"The Tawau Port plays a vital role in supporting trade, industry, and regional relations on the east coast of Sabah.
"This RM70 million investment reflects our commitment to equipping the port with the necessary infrastructure and equipment to meet future trade demands, thereby contributing to the economic development of Tawau and the surrounding area," he said.
Also present at the launch were Sabah Deputy Chief Minister III, who is also the Minister of Industrial Development, Entrepreneurship and Transport, Datuk Ewon Benedick; State Secretary Datuk Zainudin Aman, and Sabah Ports Authority chairman Datuk Donald Mojuntin.

Title: Discussions with PN in Melaka won't necessarily result in pact, says BN's Rauf
Article:
MELAKA: The winning momentum from Barisan Nasional and Perikatan Nasional's understanding in Negri Sembilan will lead to a "BN Plus" arrangement in Melaka, although discussions with PN may not necessarily result in a political pact.
Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh, who is also Melaka BN chairman, said the "BN Plus" formula reflected the state chapter's openness to negotiations with any party.
However, he said all decisions would ultimately align with BN's interests and strength in the state.
He said no coalition had been finalised, and Melaka BN remained untethered to any formal political agreement with other parties.
"We are prepared for any form of combination that we call BN Plus. Anyone can come to negotiate, but discussions will not necessarily end with an agreement or consent.
"It depends on our respective strengths. So we are not tied to any binding arrangement that has not been officially finalised.
"I am open to all parties coming to negotiate with me. If I meet anyone, do not make assumptions, because it is our right as a state to prioritise our party's interests first," he said.
He was speaking after leading the Sayang Rakyat Tour for the Telok Mas constituency.
In yesterday's Negri Sembilan election, the BN-PN pact won a two-thirds majority, securing 25 of the 36 seats.
Subsequently, BN chairman
Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi
said the coalition's understanding with PN in Negri Sembilan would continue in Melaka.
Rauf, who is also Melaka Umno chief, said BN's consecutive wins in Johor and Negri Sembilan gave the party's machinery a boost ahead of the Melaka polls.
Although the date for the Melaka state election has not been determined, he said BN's victories in the two states provided positive signals of public support.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: South Korea records highest-ever temperature of 42.5°C
Article:
SEOUL: South Korea registered its highest temperature since records began more than a century ago on Sunday, according to the state weather agency.
The southeastern city of Yangsan recorded a temperature of 42.5°C at 1.26pm (0426 GMT), the Korea Meteorological Administration (KMA) said on its website.
Yangsan has been the epicentre of the ongoing heatwave, where temperatures exceeded 40°C for a fifth consecutive day on Sunday.
Much of South Korea has been placed under heat warnings, with many cities seeing temperatures climb into the upper 30s°C.
More than 20 localities were under emergency heatwave alerts on Sunday, a new warning category introduced this year to better address rising temperatures.
An emergency alert is issued when areas experiencing a heatwave are forecast to record a perceived temperature of 38°C or an actual temperature of 39°C for one day.
KMA data show the average annual number of heatwave days in the country has more than doubled to 19 over the past five years, from eight in the 1970s.
A heatwave day is defined as one with a maximum temperature of at least 33°C, while a tropical night is one when the overnight low remains at 25°C or above.
Scientists warn that extreme weather events such as heatwaves are becoming more frequent and intense as a result of human-induced climate change.

Title: Chow: PH to review election setbacks, refine strategy
Article:
BUKIT MERTAJAM: Pakatan Harapan will hold a meeting on Aug 8 to review the causes of its defeats in the Johor and Negri Sembilan state elections and chart a new strategy ahead of the 16th General Election (GE16) and future state polls.
Penang PH chairman Chow Kon Yeow said the meeting had been scheduled before the Johor and Negri Sembilan elections as part of the coalition's early preparations should GE16 or state elections be called ahead of schedule.
"So far, we have not discussed the election results. Coincidentally, or otherwise, PH already had a meeting scheduled for Aug 8 before the Johor and Negri Sembilan elections.
"It is part of our early preparations for the possibility of an early general or state election.
"We will examine the reasons behind the Johor and Negri Sembilan results and formulate new strategies, including stepping up the use of social media to communicate our key messages," he told reporters after attending the Penang Amanah Convention here today.
Commenting on the Negri Sembilan election, Chow said the outcome had raised important questions about the country's political direction.
He said the Penang government would continue focusing on its performance, service delivery and efforts to improve the people's well-being.
"We want voters to judge us based on our achievements, how we help the people and create jobs.
"Are these no longer important? We believe they still matter.
"We will continue developing Penang while refining our strategy to retain the state's mandate," he said.
Asked whether race-based politics could undermine investor confidence, Chow said recent political developments had inevitably raised questions about Malaysia's future.
"Investors are asking about the country's direction, not just Penang's.
"They want to know whether political stability will be affected and whether Malaysia will remain a conducive destination for investment.
"These are legitimate questions arising from recent political developments and the realignment of political forces in the country," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: HLIB starts coverage on MFM with 'Buy' call
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd (HLIB) has initiated coverage on Malayan Flour Mills Bhd (MFM) with a "Buy" rating and a target price of 93 sen.
The target price is based on seven times its mid-financial year 2027 core earnings per share (EPS) estimate of 13.3 sen.
HLIB said MFM is expected to record a three-year compound annual growth rate  of 7.5 per cent in core earnings for financial years 2026 to 2028.
It said the earnings growth would be underpinned by improved operating efficiency at MFM's flour milling operations in Malaysia and Vietnam, as well as favourable input cost dynamics.
The firm said the company's integrated poultry segment is also expected to contribute to its earnings growth through margin expansion, driven by an improved product mix as MFM focuses on higher-value offerings.
This will be complemented by capacity expansion across both the upstream and downstream poultry sub-segments, it said.
HLIB also sees long-term structural growth potential in Vietnam's flour market, noting that the country's per capita wheat flour consumption remains well below regional peers, such as Malaysia and Indonesia.
It said rising household incomes, an expanding middle class and changing consumer preferences towards convenience and value-added food products should support sustained growth in Vietnam's wheat flour consumption over the medium- to long-term.
To cater to robust demand growth in Vietnam, MFM plans to expand Vimaflour's flour milling capacity by a further 25 per cent, which HLIB said would reinforce the company's leadership position in the market.
MFM is also expanding its integrated poultry platform to capitalise on long-term demand growth while supporting Malaysia's food security objectives, it added.

Title: Trump says US, Israel to hold off on Iran strikes
Article:
WASHINGTON: President Donald Trump said on Saturday that the United States and Israel had agreed to hold off on new strikes on Iran, provided a deal to end the months-long conflict is "rapidly" reached.
Fears had mounted that the fighting could escalate once again after Trump threatened to hit Iran "very hard" and was reportedly considering renewed heavy attacks, including against energy infrastructure.
Trump said the US was "locked and loaded and ready to go against the Islamic Republic of Iran", but added that Teheran and other Middle Eastern countries had asked him to hold off on fresh strikes.
"Based on this request, I have agreed, for the future benefit of the WORLD and, likewise, the survival of a successful and prosperous Iran, to cancel the attack, subject to being able to rapidly make a DEAL," Trump posted on his Truth Social platform.
The US president said the deal would have to include the "Immediate, Complete and Total OPENING OF THE HORMUZ STRAIT, and an end to Iran's nuclear threat".
"The Country of Israel joins me in this commitment. Get to work, everybody, and get it DONE."
After more than five months of war, which began on Feb 28 when the US and Israel launched strikes on Teheran, there is seemingly no end to the conflict in sight.
A previous ceasefire deal with similar terms, including the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz, fell through, and Iran has since tightened its control over the vital waterway as the two countries resumed attacks against each other in recent weeks.
The resumption of hostilities has caused global oil prices, which had dipped during the initial ceasefire, to rise again.
The back-and-forth also comes just three months before the midterm elections in the United States that could pose a challenge for Trump's Republican Party.
EAGER TO DO A DEAL
US embassies in capitals across the Middle East had warned their citizens on Saturday to beware of "unforeseen escalation" in the regional conflict and urged them to be ready to leave.
CBS News said the US and Israel were planning joint strikes, possibly throughout the weekend, with oil refineries and power plants among the possible targets.
But Trump said he ultimately decided to hold off on his threat of new attacks after requests from Gulf countries.
Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman called Trump on Saturday to express concerns about his strike plans, Axios reported, citing unnamed US officials.
One source with knowledge of the call told Axios that the Saudi crown prince had "urged Trump to de-escalate and refrain from launching the strikes".
The White House did not immediately respond to a request for comment on the report.
Iran and the US resumed exchanges of fire last month after a days-long lull in fighting, although there were no reported strikes overnight from Friday to Saturday.
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio told Fox News earlier in the week that the US had "wiped out" much of Iran's defences, adding that Teheran was "now willing and in some cases seem eager to do a deal on denuclearisation, to do a deal on the straits".
Still, he said Iran could "still do damage".
On Wednesday, a drone struck a US-owned gas vessel moored in an Egyptian port, causing a fire. Egypt is investigating but has not yet accused any group of launching the attack.
Meanwhile, an "unknown projectile" struck a tanker off the coast of Oman, a British maritime agency said on Saturday.
Iran has effectively maintained control over navigation through Hormuz since the outbreak of the war on February 28, requiring vessels to obtain permission and pay transit fees before using the waterway.
Maritime trade tracking firm Kpler said on Friday that traffic through the Hormuz Strait has dropped "sharply".
On the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, another waterway that has gained increasing importance as a transit route for Saudi Arabian oil, the Iran-backed Houthi fighters in Yemen on Saturday denied seeking to charge ships for passage through it.
The narrow waterway connects the Red Sea to the Indian Ocean and, via the Suez Canal, the Mediterranean.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Amanah eyes wider political cooperation after Negri poll losses
Article:
BUKIT MERTAJAM: Amanah will focus on strengthening political cooperation within Pakatan Harapan while exploring broader collaboration with parties that share its commitment to values-based politics.
The move comes after the party's performance in the Johor and Negri Sembilan state elections, which Amanah said warrants a comprehensive review.
Vice-president Adly Zahari said the party's priority was not merely to win more seats in future elections, but to reinforce existing alliances and build a broader political coalition.
"PH will remain the cornerstone of Amanah's political struggle, but there is room to expand cooperation with other parties that champion values-based politics.
"In previous state elections, PH worked with Muda, for example in Melaka. Going forward, we want to strengthen PH while opening more space for cooperation with parties that share similar principles, including those with Islamic and Malay-based platforms," he told reporters after opening the Penang Amanah Convention, which was also attended by Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow.
Adly said any decision on future political strategies or alliances would be made collectively within PH.
On the Negri Sembilan election, he said Amanah respected the people's mandate and would conduct a thorough post-mortem, including reviewing political cooperation and the party's organisational strength.
He maintained that the former PH-led Negri Sembilan government had delivered a strong administrative record but acknowledged that identity politics remained one of the coalition's biggest challenges.
"Race-based politics may influence voting behaviour, but it is not sustainable in the long run. Ultimately, people will return to issues that affect their daily lives, such as the cost of living, the economy and education. These are among the matters we will examine in our post-mortem to improve," he said.
Amanah failed to win any of the nine seats it contested in the Negri Sembilan election, including the Klawang state seat, which it had previously held.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Nestlé Malaysia expands ready-to-drink coffee range
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Nestle Malaysia Bhd has launched two new Nescafe ready-to-drink (RTD) coffee flavours — Spanish Latte and Tiramisu Latte — as part of its "Treat Yourself to More" campaign aimed at encouraging young Malaysians to celebrate everyday achievements.
The campaign taps into changing consumer lifestyles, where coffee has become more than just a daily beverage, serving as a way for consumers to pause and reward themselves amid increasingly busy schedules.
Nestle Malaysia business executive officer for coffee Norkhayati Mohamed Hashini said coffee has evolved into a lifestyle choice for many young Malaysians, whether they are catching up with friends or taking a break after accomplishing something.
"Through our 'Treat Yourself to More' campaign and new range of drinks inspired by café trends, we wanted to offer a simple yet delicious way to turn an everyday coffee break into something worth taking a pause and savouring," she said in a statement.
The new RTD range features Nescafe Spanish Latte, inspired by one of today's popular café beverages with smooth coffee notes and creamy sweetness, and Nescafe Tiramisu Latte, which combines coffee with creamy notes and a hint of cocoa flavour inspired by the classic dessert.
Both beverages come in 280ml bottles made from 100 per cent recycled polyethylene terephthalate (PET) and are halal-certified, offering an on-the-go option for consumers.
To mark the launch, Nescafe recently hosted a consumer event at The Campus, Ampang, attracting more than 1,800 attendees through a series of interactive activities centred on celebrating everyday achievements.
The event featured a Glambot video booth, an artificial intelligence (AI)-powered doodle station where visitors created personalised digital artwork based on their "Win of the Week", and sampling opportunities for the new beverages.
Nescafe also collaborated with Cookiecrumbs, offering visitors a "Treat Yourself to More" kit comprising either a Spanish Latte or Tiramisu Latte paired with a Cookiecrumbs cookie.
The collaboration extended to selected Cookiecrumbs outlets, where customers who spent RM25 on Cookiecrumbs products during the campaign received a complimentary Nescafe Spanish Latte or Tiramisu Latte.
Nestle Malaysia said the campaign reflects its commitment to developing products and experiences that resonate with the next generation of coffee drinkers as consumer preferences continue to evolve.
The new Nescafe RTD range is now available at major hypermarkets, supermarkets, convenience stores and on e-commerce platforms nationwide.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Restaurant kitchen fire at Sunway Square Mall put out before firefighters arrive
Article:
SUBANG JAYA: A fire involving a restaurant kitchen at the lower ground level of Sunway Square Mall in Bandar Sunway was extinguished before firemen arrived at the scene early today.
Selangor Fire and Rescue Department operations deputy director Ashrul Riezal Asbar said the department received an emergency call at 1.23am and dispatched personnel from the Subang Jaya Fire and Rescue Station.
He said the first fire engine arrived five minutes later and found the blaze had already been put out.
"The fire only involved the cooking hood in the restaurant's kitchen and did not spread to other parts of the premises.
"Our personnel carried out overhaul works and a thorough inspection to ensure there were no remaining hotspots that could reignite the fire. No casualties were reported," he said.
Ashrul said eight firefighters, assisted by a fire engine and a water tanker, were deployed to the scene.
Photographs from the scene showed the kitchen shrouded in smoke, with soot covering the cooking hood, exhaust ducting and stainless-steel workstations.
Firefighters wearing breathing apparatus inspected the kitchen and dining area to ensure the premises were safe before concluding the operation.
The cause of the fire is under investigation.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Teen placed in medically induced coma after crash with RXZ Members 8.0 participant
Article:
KUALA TERENGGANU: A 13-year-old boy who suffered burns to 60 per cent of his body in a road crash involving a participant in the RXZ Members 8.0 gathering last Friday has been placed in a medically induced coma.
The incident occurred when the motorcycle carrying the teenager and his mother was struck by another motorcycle ridden by a participant of the gathering at the Buluh Gading four-way intersection in Kuala Nerus.
The boy was placed in a medically induced coma to enable doctors to carry out procedures to clean and treat his burn wounds.
The victim's father, Talhah Mahmud, 61, said his eldest son, Ahmad Asyraf, is receiving treatment in the intensive care unit (ICU) of Sultanah Nur Zahirah Hospital (HSNZ) here, where he has been in a coma for three days.
He said although his son briefly regained consciousness on Sunday morning, doctors noted a rapid heart rate, requiring continued close monitoring.
"The attending doctors informed me that my son showed no positive response, which is deeply worrying for me.
"For now, we are concerned that his burn wounds are vulnerable to bacterial infection, as the outer layer of skin is gone and bacteria could attack those areas," he said.
He added that he was unsure how long his son would remain hospitalised, as discussions with doctors indicated treatment would take a long time.
He said he was informed that tissue needed to cover the wounds was currently unavailable, and hospital authorities were discussing options to obtain it for further treatment.
Talhah said he understood that the motorcycle ridden by his wife was struck by a Yamaha RXZ motorcycle, causing a fuel spill that triggered a fire.
"As a result of the
collision
, Ahmad Asyraf suffered 60 per cent burn injuries from the waist down, while the motorcycle ridden by my wife was destroyed and the RXZ motorcycle caught fire, sustaining about 80 per cent damage," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Man fined RM10,000 for harbouring 2 Myanmar migrants
Article:
PASIR MAS: The Sessions Court here today fined a man RM10,000 for harbouring two Myanmar undocumented migrants.
Judge Zulkpli Abdullah  fined Mohd Hilmi Admam, 42, who   pleaded guilty to the charge under under Section 55E(1) of the Immigration Act 1959/63.
Hilmi had   allowed two Myanmar men —  Varnat Thomas, 43, and Vijjay, 25 — to be in a car at Lembah Sireh bus station parking area in Kota Baru at 5.38am on July 23.
The two foreigners had committed an offence under Section 6(1)(c) of the Immigration Act 1959/63 for being in Malaysia without valid passes or permits.
Hilmi, who was unrepresented, appealed for a reduction in the fine. However, deputy public prosecutor Siti Khaidijah Khairuddin  urged the court to impose an appropriate sentence.
Zulkpli also ordered the car used in the offence to be forfeited.
Hilmi paid the  fine.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Public holiday in Negri Sembilan tomorrow, MB announces
Article:
SEREMBAN: A public holiday has been declared in Negri Sembilan tomorrow.
Newly appointed Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim said the public holiday was a gesture of appreciation to the people following Saturday's state election.
"As a mark of appreciation to the people during the state election, I declare an occasional holiday tomorrow (Aug 3)," he told a press conference at Seri Menanti Resort today.
Also present was State Secretary Datuk Mohd Zafir Ibrahim.
Earlier, Ismail, the Juasseh assemblyman, was sworn in as the new Negri Sembilan menteri besar.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Sri Lanka deploys troops after prison riot
Article:
COLOMBO: Sri Lanka deployed hundreds of troops and elite commandos on Sunday to contain riots at an overcrowded prison in which an inmate was killed and six others wounded, police said.
Deputy police inspector-general Sanjeewa Medawatte said the situation was under control after inmates destroyed multiple buildings on Saturday inside Mahara Prison, just outside the capital, Colombo.
"We got reinforcements from the armed forces and the Special Task Force commandos to restore order and send the inmates back to their cells," Medawatte told reporters outside the prison.
In November 2020, a riot erupted at the facility in which 11 inmates were shot and killed, and nearly 120 others were wounded.
[[nid:1502699]]
The latest unrest came almost a month after another prison riot in the same region, in which 10 guards and 21 inmates were killed.
Medawatte said inmates at Mahara Prison had completely destroyed the kitchen, the hospital, a newly built rehabilitation building and vocational training facilities.
The prison housed 4,100 inmates, about four times its capacity, an issue common across the country's jails.
Last month, the authorities announced plans to convert disused state buildings into prisons.
More than three-quarters of the inmates in Sri Lanka are remand prisoners awaiting trial, and most are held in connection with drug offences.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Tuanku Muhriz reminds Negri Sembilan assemblymen to put state, people before politics
Article:
KUALA PILAH: The Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negri Sembilan, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir, today reminded state assemblymen to place the interests of the state and its people above political or personal considerations.
His Royal Highness said every elected representative bears a heavy responsibility to bring the voices, aspirations, needs, and concerns of the people to the State Legislative Assembly.
Tuanku Muhriz stressed that every policy, plan, and decision made must reflect those aspirations while remaining firmly focused on the welfare of the people and the development of Negri Sembilan.
"Your loyalty and commitment must always be directed towards the state and the people you represent, taking precedence over any political or personal interests," His Royal Highness said.
Tuanku Muhriz said this during the appointment and swearing-in ceremony of the new Negri Sembilan Menteri Besar at Istana Besar Seri Menanti here today.
His Royal Highness said Negeri Sembilan requires a leadership team that remains steadfast in upholding principles and noble values, stressing that every responsibility entrusted to public office holders must be discharged with honesty, sincerity and a strong sense of accountability.
"Any abuse of power, position or the trust placed in an individual will not only tarnish the institution he or she represents, but may also lead to injustice and undermine the effective implementation of policies intended for the well-being of the people and the progress of the state," Tuanku Muhriz decreed.
Accompanying His Royal Highness at the ceremony were Tunku Ampuan Besar Tuanku Aishah Rohani Tengku Besar Mahmud, Tunku Besar Seri Menanti Tunku Ali Redhauddin Tuanku Muhriz, and Tunku Panglima Besar Tunku Zain Al-'Abidin Tuanku Muhriz.
Also present were the Undang Luak of Sungei Ujong, Datuk Klana Petra Muhammad Faris Johari and the Undang Luak of Rembau, Datuk Sedia Raja Hassan Ab Hamid.
Earlier, Juasseh assemblyman Datuk Ismail Lasim took the oath of office as the new menteri besar.
Tuanku Muhriz expressed confidence that Ismail would discharge his duties with dedication and integrity while continuing the achievements of the previous administration and addressing areas requiring further improvement.
His Royal Highness also reminded the menteri besar and all State Legislative Assembly members to remain loyal to the Royal Institution, uphold the sovereignty of the Negri Sembilan Constitution, and acknowledge the authority vested in the  Dewan Keadilan dan Undang.
Tuanku Muhriz congratulated all newly elected assemblymen on receiving the people's mandate in the 16th state election, while expressing appreciation to former assemblymen and State Executive Council members for their dedicated service during the previous term.
"To those who were unsuccessful in this election, I hope you will continue serving the people with commitment and contribute to the well-being of the community and the progress of Negri Sembilan," His Royal Highness said.
Tuanku Muhriz also urged the people to continue fostering mutual understanding, respect and appreciation for the state's rich diversity, noting that every religion, race and culture possesses noble values and traditions that should be preserved.
"I believe that by upholding the values of mutual respect, tolerance and the spirit of consensus, we will continue to strengthen unity, preserve harmony and reinforce the spirit of togetherness among our multiracial society.
"This is the essential foundation that will ensure Negri Sembilan remains peaceful, prosperous and progressive for the benefit of both present and future generations," His Royal Highness said.
Election Commission Chairman Datuk Seri Ramlan Harun yesterday announced that Barisan Nasional won 18 of the 36 state seats, while Pakatan Harapan secured 11 seats and Perikatan Nasional won seven.
The new Negri Sembilan state government was subsequently formed through a collaboration between BN and PN.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Steven Sim calls for self-reflection after Negri election, says every poll offers lessons
Article:
BUKIT MERTAJAM: Penang DAP chairman Steven Sim described the Negri Sembilan election results as a timely reminder for the party to reflect, regroup and strengthen its strategy ahead of future political challenges.
He said every election offered valuable lessons, but noted that DAP remained proud of retaining nine state seats, while Pakatan Harapan secured 11 seats overall in Negri Sembilan.
"We thank the people of Negri Sembilan for taking part in the election and for exercising their democratic right to vote.
"It was never an easy contest. We knew from the very beginning that we would face significant challenges. Still, we are proud of the courageous leadership shown by Anthony Loke in leading our campaign in Negri Sembilan.
"In the end, we secured nine seats. We must take a self-reflective stance or approach, as there are lessons to be learnt in every election," he told reporters here today.
Earlier, he officiated the 2026 Entrepreneur Development and Cooperatives Ministty Madani Sales Programme at the Taman Makok Basketball Court here, which was also attended by Angkatan Koperasi Kebangsaan Malaysia Berhad (Angkasa) president Datuk Seri Dr Abdul Fattah Abdullah, who is also Umno deputy permanent chairman.
Asked whether the Negri Sembilan result signalled a tougher battle for PH in Penang should the state election be held there, Sim said the party's focus was not on political confidence but on consistently serving the people.
He stressed that election campaigning does not begin only when the state assembly is dissolved, but starts immediately after the previous election.
"My instruction has always been the same — work hard to retain the people's trust and confidence. Our work begins the day after the last election. Those who won must continue serving on the ground without compromise, while those who lost must work even harder to regain public support," he said.
Sim said Penang PH remained focused on delivering the best service to the people and was prepared for future electoral contests.
"We must close ranks and stay united. We must continue working hard on the ground. I am confident the people will judge us based on the performance of the state government, the federal government and our elected representatives," he said.
On concerns that voting patterns were becoming increasingly polarised along racial lines, Sim said Malaysia's strength lay in its multiracial society and that any government must serve all communities equally.
"No government can prioritise only one race. You cannot say only the Chinese, Malays or Indians matter.
"It is like in a family — you cannot only look after the youngest child just because people say the youngest is pampered. If you give everything only to the youngest, there will be resentment.
"So if you want to maintain unity in a multiracial society, any government must adopt an approach that safeguards racial harmony and unity. That is my stand," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: RXZ Members 8.0 roars to record 200,000 turnout
Article:
KUALA NERUS: The RXZ Members 8.0 gathering made history by drawing more than 200,000 participants, the largest turnout since its inception in 2017.
RXZ Members 8.0 organiser Mohamad Faizal Mat Ali said the turnout surpassed last year's record of 160,000 participants.
Organisers had initially expected attendance to drop by 10 per cent as the event coincided with polling day for the Negri Sembilan election.
Faizal said this year's gathering drew Yamaha RXZ fans from across the country, as well as participants from several neighbouring countries.
He said the international turnout proved that the RXZ Members brand was growing in prominence and attracting attention from the global motoring community.
"Riders of other motorcycle brands and models also attended to experience the excitement, meet friends and join various activities," he said at the Terengganu Motor Racing Track in Gong Badak.
The three-day RXZ Members 8.0 event, which ended yesterday, brought together Yamaha RXZ enthusiasts through various activities, including motorcycle exhibitions, merchandise sales, lucky draws and community networking sessions.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: High Court stay on medicine price display order still in force, says MMA
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysian Medical Association (MMA) has clarified that the High Court's stay on the enforcement of the medicine price display order against private clinics remains in force.
The association said this follows reports of enforcement officers visiting private clinics in several states to request price lists, despite the stay on the Price Control and Anti-Profiteering (Price Marking for Drug) Order 2025.
The government did not appeal against the stay, meaning it remains active while the judicial review is pending.
"No compound, prosecution or other enforcement action should be taken against private medical or dental practitioners for non-compliance with this order while the court proceedings are ongoing," said Malaysian Medical Association president Datuk Dr Thirunavukarasu Rajoo in a statement.
He said this does not prevent authorities from carrying out their lawful duties under other legislation, but inspections should not be used to enforce the medicine price display order, directly or indirectly.
He called on the Health Ministry and the Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Ministry to issue clear and consistent instructions to enforcement officers nationwide, saying private practitioners should not face confusion or anxiety due to differing interpretations at the state level.
He advised practitioners to cooperate professionally with lawful inspections, while asking that any threatened compound or enforcement action specifically related to the medicine price display order be documented and reported to the association immediately.
"The substantive judicial review remains before the High Court, and the legal process must be respected," he said.
The High Court granted the stay in May, pending disposal of a judicial review filed by the
association
and other private practitioner groups challenging the order.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Aminuddin preparing to vacate Negri MB's official residence
Article:
SEREMBAN: Datuk Seri Aminuddin Harun is preparing to vacate the Negri Sembilan menteri besar's official residence following his defeat in last night's state election.
It is understood that Aminuddin is making final preparations to move out and is expected to leave at any time.
The Pakatan Harapan Negri Sembilan chairman lost the
Linggi state seat
after opting not to defend Sikamat, which he won in 2023 with a 2,662-vote majority.
Barisan Nasional and Perikatan Nasional won a combined
25 seats

Title: Elderly man braves three-hour journey to fulfil wife's wish to visit Karnival Jom Heboh Sarawak
Article:
KOTA SAMARAHAN: An elderly man braved a three-hour journey from Maludam to bring his family to Karnival Jom Heboh Sarawak Segulai Sejalai here today, fulfilling his wife's long-cherished dream.
Untong Mahidin, 69, travelled from Betong with his wife, Alawiyah Jon, 67, and their two children, aged 24 and 35, so she could experience the carnival's vibrant atmosphere firsthand.
He said his wife has suffered from knee pain and health issues for nearly a decade, leaving her unable to walk and rarely able to travel far from home.
When she heard the event was taking place in Kota Samarahan, she expressed excitement after years of listening to relatives and friends speak about the carnival.
"She was truly excited. All this while, she only heard people talk about it, especially when two previous Jom Heboh events were held in Kuching. People said there was so much to see, so I asked our two children to accompany us on this trip.
"We came to Kota Samarahan solely to see Jom Heboh. There were no other errands; I just wanted to fulfil my wife's wish," he said when met at the site today.
Untong said they had previously hoped to attend, but the six-hour journey from their village proved too long and exhausting.
However, the opening of the Batang Lupar Bridge last month cut their travel time in half to about three hours, making the trip possible.
"Alhamdulillah, travel is much easier now. With the journey shortened, I thought this was the best opportunity to bring my wife to see for herself what she had only heard about from others," he said.
Despite spending only about two hours at the carnival grounds before leaving at noon, Untong said the visit brought immense joy to his family.
"We are truly satisfied. What people say is true — there is so much to see at Jom Heboh. Even though it was brief, at least my wife's wish came true and she got to experience the atmosphere here," he said.
The family then made the three-hour journey back to their village, carrying memories that Alawiyah will cherish after years of hearing about the event from others.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Lawyers group urges police to probe Rocky's death under Animal Welfare Act
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR:  Lawyers for Animal Rights (LFAR) has urged police to investigate the death of a dog known as Rocky under the Animal Welfare Act 2015 instead of the Penal Code, arguing that the case concerns animal cruelty rather than damage to property.
LFAR founder Rajesh Nagarajan said Section 428 of the Penal Code, which deals with mischief, treats sentient animals as property.
"Investigating Rocky's death under the provision would effectively treat the dog as property instead of recognising it as a living creature capable of suffering.
"Parliament enacted the Animal Welfare Act 2015 specifically to address such cases, namely Section 29, which criminalises the infliction of unnecessary pain or suffering, and Section 30, which prohibits the killing of an animal except under specific statutory exceptions," he said in a statement today.
Rajesh urged police to publicly explain why the investigation was not being conducted under the Animal Welfare Act, adding that the involvement of local council enforcement officers during a stray dog capture operation did not make any alleged act of cruelty lawful.
"All parties involved, including residents, contractors, enforcement officers and officials, should be investigated and prosecuted under the Animal Welfare Act if evidence supports such action
"Failing to invoke the Act would send the wrong message by suggesting that acts of cruelty committed during official operations would be treated more leniently than intended by Parliament," he said.
LFAR also cited the statement by the Tengku Permaisuri of Selangor, who had said that no individual, contractor, enforcement officer or government agency was above the law in cases involving animal cruelty and had called for a thorough investigation and appropriate legal action under the Animal Welfare Act.
https://www.nst.com.my/news/nation/2026/08/1502609/dvs-files-police-report-records-statements-rocky-abuse-probe
The statement comes after the Selangor Department of Veterinary Services (DVS) confirmed it had lodged a police report and recorded statements from the suspect and several witnesses over Rocky's death.
DVS said the case is being investigated under Section 29(1)(e) of the Animal Welfare Act 2015, following a viral video allegedly showing the dog being tied and dragged by its neck during a stray dog capture operation in Taman Teluk Gedung Indah, Port Klang, on July 29.
Upon conviction, the offence carries a fine of between RM20,000 and RM100,000, imprisonment of up to three years, or both.

Title: Ismail: Appointment as MB is a huge responsibility
Article:
KUALA PILAH: New Negri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim says his appointment is a huge responsibility.
He said he recognised that the post was not a privilege to be boasted about, but a duty that must be carried out with sincerity, loyalty, honesty, wisdom and a high sense of accountability.
"I humbly offer my utmost gratitude to Your Royal Highness for the trust and consent bestowed upon me to undertake this duty as Negri Sembilan menteri besar," he said when taking his oath before the Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negri Sembilan, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir, today.
Also present at the ceremony at Istana Besar Seri Menanti were Tunku Ampuan Besar Negri Sembilan Tuanku Aishah Rohani Tengku Besar Mahmud, Tunku Besar Seri Menanti Tunku Ali Redhauddin and Tunku Panglima Besar Tunku Zain Al'Abidin.
Others in attendance included Undang Luak Sungei Ujong Datuk Muhammad Faris Johari and Undang Luak Rembau Datuk Hassan Ab Hamid, along with Barisan Nasional deputy chairman Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan and Negri Sembilan elected representatives.
Ismail expressed his gratitude to the people of Negri Sembilan for fulfilling their democratic duty and giving their mandate to BN and Perikatan Nasional in yesterday's state election.
He said his appointment came with the obligation to prove that the state government would work diligently, listen to the people and carry out its duties fairly, transparently and effectively.
The Juasseh assemblyman also thanked his predecessor, former menteri besar Datuk Seri Aminuddin Harun, for his service, contributions, leadership and dedication throughout his tenure.
He said the foundation built by Aminuddin, who had served as menteri besar since 2018, would serve as a valuable platform to continue the progress and prosperity of Negri Sembilan.
Ismail pledged to uphold the dignity of the royal institution and defend the principles of the Federal Constitution and the Negri Sembilan constitution.
"I will also always uphold the royal decrees, advice, views and guidance of Your Royal Highness in carrying out all matters and duties of the state government administration," he said.

Title: Who is Negri Sembilan's new Menteri Besar, Datuk Ismail Lasim?
Article:
SEREMBAN: After more than two decades representing Juasseh, veteran Umno leader Datuk Ismail Lasim was sworn in today as the 12th
Menteri Besar of Negri Sembilan
.
The appointment and oath-taking ceremony was held at the Balairung Seri of Istana Besar Seri Menanti before the Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negri Sembilan, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir.
Ismail, 67, succeeds Datuk Seri Aminuddin Harun after Barisan Nasional, with the support of Perikatan Nasional, secured a majority of 25 seats in the 36-seat state assembly to form the new state government.
A long-serving Umno leader, Ismail has represented Juasseh since 1999, making him one of the longest-serving assemblymen in the state.
He retained the seat in the recent state election with a 4,323-vote majority, defeating Bersatu's Mohd Zuhaimi Md Yusof and Pakatan Harapan's Mohd Aidil Abdullah.
A law graduate from Universiti Malaya, Ismail began his career as an advocate and solicitor with Messrs Halim & Ismail between 1995 and 1997 before moving into politics.
Within Umno, he currently serves as the party's Negri Sembilan liaison committee information chief and deputy chairman, while also leading the Kuala Pilah Umno division, a position he has held since 2001.
He previously served as the state Umno liaison committee treasurer and was also the former deputy chief of Negri Sembilan Umno Youth.
Before taking the state's top leadership role, Ismail served as a member of the Negri Sembilan state executive council, overseeing the education and human capital portfolio from 2023 until the dissolution of the state assembly.
He had also previously held the infrastructure, water, energy and telecommunications portfolio, where he chaired the State Road Safety Council and served as deputy chairman of the State Planning Committee.
His other responsibilities included serving on the State Action Committee for Information, Industry, Investment and Islamic Affairs, as well as sitting on the board of Syarikat Air Negri Sembilan.
Ismail has also chaired the Kuala Pilah District Development Action Committee, a role that placed him close to grassroots development issues in the district.
His appointment marks Umno's return to the Menteri Besar's office after Pakatan Harapan governed the state for two terms under Aminuddin, who served as Menteri Besar from 2018.
The change in leadership follows BN's strong performance in the state election, where the coalition won 18 seats, while PH secured 11 and PN seven.
With PN's support, BN now commands a comfortable majority in the state assembly as Ismail begins his tenure leading Negri Sembilan's new administration.

Title: Only one-third of Malaysia-US exports face new tariff
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Only about one-third of Malaysia's exports to the United States will be subject to the new 10 per cent tariff under the US Trade Representative's (USTR) latest Section 301 action, according to CIMB Securities Sdn Bhd.
The firm estimated that 31.9 per cent of Malaysia's exports to the US will be subject to the Section 301 tariff, down from 33 per cent under the previous Section 122 regime.
CIMB Securities said this would move an estimated RM3.3 billion of Malaysian exports out of the tariff's scope and lower the trade-weighted effective tariff rate to 5.1 per cent from 5.2 per cent.
The 10 per cent tariff on Malaysian goods took effect on July 24, replacing the 10 per cent tariff imposed under Section 122, which expired on the same day after reaching its maximum 150-day duration.
The USTR's final action followed its investigation into forced labour practices in 60 economies, including Malaysia.
The agency said the tariffs were intended to encourage countries to eliminate practices deemed actionable under Section 301.
CIMB Securities said Malaysia and Indonesia were assigned a 10 per cent rate, compared with 12.5 per cent for Thailand and Singapore, reflecting commitments made by Malaysia and Indonesia under their respective agreements with the US on forced labour import prohibitions.
Malaysia also received country-specific exemptions for palm oil, palm kernel oil, oleochemicals and wood products, among other products.
Of the newly exempted exports, about RM2.1 billion comprises palm oil, palm kernel oil, oleochemicals and plywood, while most of the remainder consists of semiconductor measuring and testing instruments added to the universal exemption list.
CIMB Securities said rubber gloves remain the largest tariffed product group, with about RM6.5 billion of exports subject to the duty, followed by printing machinery parts and medical instruments at about RM4.5 billion each.
However, the firm expects Malaysia's tariff exposure to rise after a separate Section 301 investigation into structural excess capacity concludes.
The investigation covers 16 economies, including Malaysia, Indonesia, Singapore and Thailand.
Public hearings were held in May, but the USTR has yet to publish its findings or proposed measures.
CIMB Securities said it continued to expect additional tariffs following the investigation, potentially lifting Malaysia's headline tariff rate back towards the 15 to 19 per cent range.
It said the forced labour action leaves Malaysia's tariff exposure largely unchanged from the previous Section 122 regime, but this could change once excess-capacity tariffs are imposed.

Title: Message from voters clear, we'll work hard to regain support, says DAP
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: DAP has pledged to rebuild and move forward after accepting the outcome of the Negri Sembilan election, acknowledging that voters had sent a clear message to the party.
DAP national chairman Gobind Singh Deo said the party accepted the result with humility and thanked voters who supported Pakatan Harapan and DAP, as well as its candidates, members, volunteers and campaign workers.
"The message from the electorate is clear. We must and will undertake a thorough assessment of the outcome, listen carefully to the concerns of the people and work hard to regain their confidence and support," he said in a statement today.
Gobind also acknowledged the defeat of DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke in Chennah following a closely fought contest.
He said Loke had served the party and the people with distinction over many years, expressing confidence that he would continue contributing to the party and public service.
"DAP has faced setbacks before. The message from the electorate is clear. We must and will undertake a thorough assessment of the outcome."
Gobind said the party respected the mandate given by voters and congratulated those elected to form the next Negri Sembilan state government.
"We hope they will govern responsibly and always place the interests of the people first."
The Negri Sembilan election saw Barisan Nasional emerge as the largest bloc with 18 seats, followed by PH with 11 seats and Perikatan Nasional with seven.
DAP remained PH's strongest-performing component in the state, winning eight seats, but the defeat of Loke — one of the party's key national figures — has raised questions over its wider appeal and grassroots connection.
The party is expected to face renewed discussions over its strategy, leadership direction and efforts to expand beyond its traditional support base as it prepares for its national congress on Aug 16.

Title: AI keeps consumer prices high in 'RAMaggedon' chip crunch
Article:
HONG KONG: Print-outs of articles about the global memory chip shortage are pinned beside a price list at a Hong Kong computer shop, offering an explanation to confused customers feeling the pinch.
Price rises for goods such as laptops and smartphones, with cars potentially next, have been an unwelcome side-effect of the artificial intelligence gold rush - and the squeeze is far from over.
Samsung Electronics' chief financial officer said this week that shortages of microchips that store digital data will likely deepen in 2027 and remain tight through 2028.
The crunch has been nicknamed "RAMaggedon" after the components called RAM, or "random-access memory".
It is caused as profit-hungry chipmakers pivot to producing high-bandwidth memory (HBM) - a more advanced type of computer memory in huge demand to help train and run AI tools.
The articles on display at In-Technology Services - one of many compact vendors crammed into Hong Kong's Wan Chai Computer Centre - are to inform customers who "don't know what happened", manager Wade Lam told AFP.
The centre's shops sell tech equipment of all sorts, from computer parts to gadgets and games consoles.
Ken Tam, manager of Videocom Computer, which specialises in custom-built PCs, said business has halved since price rises began in September.
Sixteen gigabytes of RAM used to cost HK$300-400 ($40-50) but the price has now hit HK$1,500, he said.
"When it suddenly gets so expensive, customers have a psychological barrier," Tam told AFP.
"If they need it, they will buy it," but otherwise they will wait or "lower their standards" and buy a lower-performing memory chip, he said.
Chinese competition
Analyst Ellie Wang at the Taiwan-based market research firm TrendForce said memory prices for PCs and smartphones were up around five to six times compared to a year ago.
The AI boom has brought humungous profits and share price jumps to the world's top three memory chip makers: South Korea's Samsung Electronics and SK hynix, along with US giant Micron.
In fourth place is ChangXin Memory Technologies (CXMT), which became mainland China's most valuable company on Monday when it made its market debut in Shanghai -- another sign of how red-hot the sector has become.
CXMT, as a relative newcomer, "remains in a follower position regarding leading-edge technologies", James Zhao, senior principal analyst at Omdia, told AFP.
HBM is used in data centre servers to support other powerful chips – such as those made by US titan Nvidia –  that execute the dizzyingly complex calculations of AI systems.
But when it comes to conventional RAM, and a type for computers called DRAM, "the current supply-constrained market environment" could bring CXMT "late-mover advantages", he said.
At a shopping centre in a different part of Hong Kong, customer Henry Wong, an investment banker, said he had chosen to upgrade the RAM in an older laptop instead of buying a new one with even better specifications.
"After upgrading the memory, I found it ran really smoothly, and I stopped wanting to buy a new computer," he told AFP.
'Bubble'
Automakers say they are facing rising costs for in-vehicle computer systems, which could also soon push up the price of new vehicles.
In Tokyo's tech hub of Akihabara, Charles Brousse, a 30-year-old graphic designer and custom PC builder from Belgium, said prices for RAM, graphics cards and motherboards have hit "ridiculous levels".
For his "PC & Chill" service, Brousse does not buy parts to pre-build machines – as it is too expensive –  but requires clients to purchase their own, which he then assembles.
The chip shortage is pushing people to buy cheaper laptops than desktops, which can last up to a decade, said Brousse, who was in Tokyo on his honeymoon.
"I'm not sure that's a good thing; people end up buying products with shorter lifespans, which fuels a cycle of consumption."
Brousse added that the fact it is driven by the "speculative bubble" of AI is also frustrating, "because I'm a graphic designer by trade, so AI has a real impact on my profession."

Title: Police hunt suspects involved in public brawl at Pandamaran sports complex
Article:
KLANG: Police are tracking down several people following a public brawl involving a 16-year-old schoolboy at the Pandamaran Sports Complex here.
South Klang district police chief Assistant Commissioner Lim Jit Huey said police detected a video uploaded on Facebook showing two males fighting while being watched by a group of men.
"Investigations found that the incident occurred at 1.20pm on July 31 at the sports complex's parking area.
"One of those involved is a 16-year-old school student, while the identity of the other male has yet to be established," he said.
He added that the cause of the incident is still under investigation and police are tracing all individuals involved in the fight.
Lim said the South Klang district Criminal Investigation Department had opened an investigation paper under Section 160 of the Penal Code for committing an affray.
The offence carries a jail term of up to six months, a fine of up to RM1,000, or both.
The case is also being investigated under Section 233 of the Communications and Multimedia Act 1998 for improper use of network facilities or services, which carries a jail term of up to one year or a fine.
Those with information can contact investigating officer Inspector Mohammad Baaz Mohd Zohari at 016-411 7885, the South Klang district police operations room at 03-3376 2222, or the nearest police station.

Title: BN's win a mandate to revitalise Negri, says Azalina
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Barisan Nasional's victory in the Negri Sembilan election is a mandate to revitalise the state, said Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said.
The Umno information chief said the win was not merely a cause for celebration, but a responsibility for BN to govern better and deliver on its manifesto effectively.
"The political understanding between BN and Perikatan Nasional in Negeri Sembilan was also one of the key foundations of this success," she said in a statement.
"The decision to avoid multi-cornered contests demonstrated that political maturity, strategic discipline and clarity of purpose can provide the people with a more organised electoral choice," she said.
Azalina also said that successful campaigns required more than traditional ceramah, posters and party machinery.
"They also require the ability to understand the issues, gauge public sentiment, harness data and craft the right narrative," she said.
She thanked Negri Sembilan voters for their trust while congratulating BN chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi, deputy chairman Datuk Seri Utama Mohamad Hasan, and all candidates and party workers.
Azalina added that with the campaign over, the focus must shift to serving all Negri Sembilan residents regardless of race, religion, constituency or political affiliation.
"The time has now come to fulfil the mandate entrusted to us and prove worthy of the confidence placed in Barisan Nasional," she said.

Title: Ismail Lasim sworn in as new Negri Sembilan Menteri Besar [WATCH]
Article:
SEREMBAN: Juasseh assemblyman Datuk Ismail Lasim has been sworn in as the 12th Menteri Besar of Negri Sembilan.
Ismail, 67, took his oath of office before the Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negri Sembilan, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir, at the Balairung Seri (Throne Room) of Istana Besar Seri Menanti at 11.29am.
Also in attendance were Tunku Ampuan Besar Tuanku Aishah Rohani Tengku Besar Mahmud, Tunku Besar Seri Menanti Tunku Ali Redhauddin Tuanku Muhriz, and Tunku Panglima Besar Tunku Zain Al-'Abidin Tuanku Muhriz.
The ceremony was also attended by the Undang Luak of Sungai Ujong, Datuk Klana Petra Muhammad Faris Johari, and the Undang Luak of Rembau, Datuk Sedia Raja Hassan Ab Hamid.
Barisan Nasional deputy chairman Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan and other state elected representatives were also present.
Ismail was among several names previously shortlisted by BN for the state's top post, alongside Negri Sembilan Umno chairman and Pertang assemblyman Datuk Seri Jalaluddin Alias, Lenggeng assemblyman Datuk Mohd Asna Amin and Johol assemblyman Datuk Saiful Yazan Sulaiman.
In the 16th Negri Sembilan election, Ismail retained the Juasseh seat for BN, defeating Bersatu's Mohd Zuhaimi Md Yusof and Pakatan Harapan's (PH) Mohd Aidil Abdullah with a 4,323-vote majority.
BN won 18 of the 36 state seats, while Perikatan Nasional (PN) secured seven, allowing the two coalitions to form the new state government with a combined 25-seat majority.
Ismail, who is also Negeri Sembilan Umno information chief, holds a Bachelor of Laws (LLB Hons) degree from Universiti Malaya.
Born in Kampung Tebing Tinggi, Juasseh, he received his early education at Sekolah Kebangsaan Pusat Juasseh and King George V School in Seremban before pursuing higher studies at Universiti Malaya.
He has served as an assemblyman for Senaling and Juasseh since 1999 and previously held the state executive councillor portfolio for education under former Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan and later Datuk Seri Aminuddin Harun.
Ismail has also held various leadership roles, including chairman of the Negri Sembilan Road Safety Committee, member of the state Islamic Affairs, Information, Industry and Investment Action Committee, board member of Syarikat Air Negeri Sembilan and chairman of the Kuala Pilah District Development Action Committee.

Title: Ismail Lasim set to become Negri Sembilan MB?
Article:
KUALA PILAH: Juasseh assemblyman Datuk Ismail Lasim is expected to be sworn in as the new Negri Sembilan Menteri Besar today following Barisan Nasional's victory in the state election.
Sources said Ismail was among several names submitted by BN for consideration, alongside state Umno liaison committee chairman Datuk Seri Jalaluddin Alias, Lenggeng assemblyman Datuk Mohd Asna Amin and Johol assemblyman Datuk Saiful Yazan Sulaiman.
Ismail, 63, retained the Juasseh seat in the 16th Negri Sembilan election, defeating Bersatu's Mohd Zuhaimi Md Yusof and Pakatan Harapan's Mohd Aidil Abdullah with a majority of 4,323 votes.
BN secured 18 seats in the 36-seat state assembly, allowing the coalition to form the new state government with the support of Perikatan Nasional, which won seven seats.
The appointment would mark a return of Umno-led leadership in Negri Sembilan after PH previously governed the state with BN as its partner under the unity arrangement at the federal level.

Title: Don't repeat past mistakes, Asyraf tells Umno after Negri win
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Umno secretary-general Datuk Dr Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki has called on party members and supporters to remain humble following Barisan Nasional's victory in the Negri Sembilan election, urging them not to repeat past mistakes of arrogance after securing the people's mandate.
Asyraf said there was no longer a need to attack or ridicule defeated opponents, stressing that the party's focus should now be on fulfilling the responsibility entrusted by voters with sincerity and humility.
"There is no need to continue criticising, let alone insulting, those who have lost, despite the pain of being subjected to slander and accusations during the campaign.
"Do not repeat past mistakes. Stay away from arrogance. Now, focus on carrying out the people's mandate with sincerity and humility," he said in a Facebook post today.
His remarks came after BN, led by Umno, emerged as the
biggest winner
in the Negri Sembilan election, securing 18 seats, including 16 won by Umno.
The result marked a significant turnaround for the party, which contested the election as part of a broader political landscape shaped by the BN-Perikatan Nasional understanding that helped prevent vote splitting among Malay voters.
Asyraf's remarks also appeared aimed at reinforcing BN's message that electoral gains must translate into responsible governance, rather than renewed political confrontation.
The Negri Sembilan result saw Pakatan Harapan secure 11 seats, while PN won seven.
The outcome has triggered debate over changing voter preferences, particularly among Malay voters, and the future direction of opposition parties including Bersatu.
